findings.title: Unchanged installed cron fails every cutover rerun
findings.description: `production_changes()` strips the new arguments from `new` but not `old`. After the first apply, both contain the new arguments, so even identical cron files produce differences. Verified by calling the helper with identical post-cutover input. Any recovery rerun therefore stops in `step_apply`, before reaching unfinished steps. Normalize both sides and add a post-cutover rerun regression test.

findings.title: Weekly backup cannot resume after a downstream failure
findings.description: The skip condition requires both today's base backup and the arm file. If the backup succeeds but its upload, catch-up push, or reconcile guards fail, today's backup remains while the arm file is absent. Rerunning invokes the full weekly command again, but `scripts/backup_prod.sh` explicitly rejects an existing destination. Implement a verified resume path that retries unfinished stages without recreating the backup, and test this partial-success case.

findings.title: Failed health invocation can pass using an old log entry
findings.description: `run_health()` ignores the subprocess result and reads the last existing log entry without verifying that this invocation appended it. If the command fails before writing—for example, because the script cannot execute—an earlier `FLAGS archive=0 stale=0` entry still passes both health gates. Require fresh output from the current invocation and validate its execution status while preserving the first check's intentional tolerance of stale-backup alarms. Add a regression test with a failed command and an existing clean log.
